## 0. Deadlines. Read this before anything else.

Generated by `build_slot_deadlines()` (`R/42_deadlines.R`) against the POST-MOVE roster.

**A slot's deadline is not the starter's kickoff.** It is bounded by the earliest
kickoff among players who could legally replace him. Week 2 got this wrong for Adams
by 31 hours.

| slot | player | own kickoff | **all options until** | any change until | binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QB | Mahomes | Sun 13:00 | **Sun 13:00** | Sun 13:00 | own kickoff |
| K | **Butker** | Sun 13:00 | **Sun 13:00** | Sun 13:00 | forced, no bench K |
| DEF | **Chiefs** | Sun 13:00 | **Sun 13:00** | Sun 13:00 | forced, no bench DEF |
| RB | Henry | Sun 16:25 | **Sun 13:00** | Sun 16:05 | replacement |
| RB | J. Williams | Sun 16:25 | **Sun 13:00** | Sun 16:05 | replacement |
| FLEX | Etienne | Sun 16:25 | **Sun 13:00** | **Sun 16:25** | replacement |
| WR | Adams | Sun 20:20 | **Sun 13:00** | Sun 20:20 | replacement |
| WR | Sutton | Sun 20:20 | **Sun 13:00** | Sun 20:20 | replacement |
| TE | Ferguson | Sun 16:25 | Sun 16:25 | Sun 16:25 | forced, no bench TE |

**The K slot moved 3h05m EARLIER** as a side effect of the Butker move: McLaughlin was
Sun 16:05, Butker is Sun 13:00. Nobody asked for that and nothing was lost — the slot is
forced either way — but it is exactly the class of thing the deadline table exists to
surface. **Eight of nine slots now want a decision by Sun 13:00.**

## 1. Correlation. NEW and self-inflicted. Record it honestly.

**Three starters are now in one game: Mahomes + Butker + Chiefs DEF, KC @ MIA, Sun 13:00.**
Plus J. Williams + Ferguson in BAL @ DAL. Five of nine starters in two games.

This was not a decision. It is the *residue* of two decisions each made on its own
merits, and neither considered the other. Naming it because Week 2 §3 set this up as the
one learnable signal and it would be dishonest to only flag correlation when it hurts.

**Why it is probably fine here, stated in advance so the retro can test it:**
1. KC is favored by **11.5**, the largest spread on the slate. The scenario that sinks
   all three at once — KC in a low-scoring loss — is the one the market prices lowest.
2. MIA's passing game is missing **Tyreek Hill (knee, ACL)** plus three WRs `Q`. MIA
   implied **17.5**, lowest on the board.
3. QB and K on the same team are *partial substitutes* within a drive — a TD pays the QB
   4 and the K 1, a FG pays the QB ~0 and the K 3 — so they are less correlated than
   the shared uniform suggests.

**Contrast worth keeping.** Earlier this week a Stafford-for-Mahomes swap was rejected
partly for stacking Stafford with Adams. That stack *cost* 4.25 projected points to buy
correlation. This KC concentration *gained* 3.58. Same variance logic, opposite price.
Correlation is not the thing to avoid — **paying for it** is.

**Kill condition:** all three of Mahomes, Butker, Chiefs finish under 60% of projection
(12.54 / 5.44 / 4.66). That is one game script sinking three slots, and it would mean
single-game concentration needs a real penalty, not just a flag.

### 1a. Head-to-head overlap. Only visible once the opponent lineup was logged.

**Eight of my nine starters sit in three games**, and the opponent has players in two of
them. This changes the shape of the margin, not just my own variance.

| game | when | mine | theirs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BAL @ DAL** | Sun 16:25 | Henry 16.99, J. Williams 13.32, Ferguson 7.57 = **37.88** | **L. Jackson 22.89** |
| **KC @ MIA** | Sun 13:00 | Mahomes 20.90, Butker 9.06, Chiefs 7.77 = **37.73** | — |
| **LA @ DEN** | Sun 20:20 | Adams 9.89, Sutton 8.81 = **18.70** | Rams DEF 5.77 |

Two genuine hedges fell out of this, neither of them planned:

**BAL @ DAL is self-damping.** Henry and their Lamar Jackson are **teammates**. Baltimore
scoring helps Henry *and* Jackson; my Williams and Ferguson are on the other side. Any
Baltimore blowout moves ~38 of my points and ~23 of theirs in partly offsetting
directions. The margin is less sensitive to this game than 60 points of exposure suggests.

**Sutton is directly opposed to their Rams DEF.** Denver's passing game succeeding is the
same event as the Rams defense failing. Points I gain there are points they lose.

**KC @ MIA is the unhedged one.** 37.73 of my points, none of theirs. It is my biggest
single-game bet and the one with no offset — which is the §1 concentration restated in
head-to-head terms, and the reason the kill condition above is worth checking.

**Consequence for the retro:** margin variance is lower than either roster's standalone
variance implies. Do not read a close final score as evidence the projections were sharp.

## 2. Decisions

### D1. QB — Mahomes starts, Stafford benched

Deadline **Sun 13:00** (Mahomes' own kickoff; Stafford is Sun 20:20, so the swap dies
when KC kicks). Proj **20.90 vs 16.65**.

**Call:** Mahomes.
**Reason:** +4.25 proj, and the matchup is the best on the slate — KC favored by 11.5,
implied **29.0**. The "blowout risk caps his ceiling" worry was tested against 2024-25
and is **false**: QBs favored by 10+ score **1.120x their own season average** (n=37).
A big spread mostly means a bad opponent, and that beats the resting risk.

Also tested and rejected: Stafford as an underdog variance play stacked with Adams. It
loses under every assumption set tried, because 4.25 points of mean is too much to buy
back with correlation.

**Kill condition:** Stafford outscores Mahomes by >4.
**Weaker signal:** Stafford by 0-4 -> noise.

### D2. WR — Adams + Sutton start, Odunze benched

Deadline **Sun 13:00** for the full option set. Proj: Adams 9.91, Sutton 8.82,
Odunze 7.69, Robinson 7.28, Raymond 4.94.

**Call:** Adams and Sutton, unchanged from Week 2.
**Reason:** highest two projections, and **game script does not move WR scoring** —
measured 2024-25, receivers run 0.94-1.06x their own average across every spread bucket,
because trailing teams pass more and that offsets the lost possessions. So Sutton being
on a 2.5-point underdog is **not** a reason to bench him, and Adams being on a favorite
is not a reason to start him. The projections decide it, and they are close.

**This is the decision Week 2 got wrong** (D2 fired: Sutton 4.00, Odunze 5.80, and
Odunze's snap share went 48% -> 84%). Re-examined rather than re-run: Odunze's Week 3
projection (7.69) is *below* Sutton's (8.82) even after Yahoo saw that snap share, and
Chicago plays **Monday** — so if Sutton is inactive Sunday, Odunze is still available.
The option is kept, not spent.

**Kill condition:** Odunze outscores BOTH Adams and Sutton. Beating one is variance.

### D3. FLEX — Etienne holds, but he is `Q`

Deadline: full options **Sun 13:00**, any change **Sun 16:25**. Proj **9.70**.

**Call:** start Etienne, with a live contingency.
**Reason:** NO favored by 3.5, which is the **peak RB bucket** measured on 2024-25 —
running backs on 3-7 point favorites score **1.078x** their own average, the best of any
game-script bucket. He is also the highest-projected FLEX option by 2.01.

**Week 2 D4 fired on him** (6.10 pts, opportunity 18 -> 10) and the "opportunity is
sticky" thesis failed at n=2. Holding anyway because the environment reversed: Week 2 was
a 19.5-implied road game as a 7.5-point dog; Week 3 is 23.5 implied at home as a favorite.

**LIVE CONTINGENCY — this is the highest-value action of the week.**
Etienne is `Q` (hamstring), confirmed in both `yahoo_week3_injuries.csv` and
`yahoo_week3_gamedaycalls.csv`. Inactives drop **~Sun 14:55** for the 16:25 games.
Odunze and Raymond play **Mon 20:15**, so they stay swappable until Etienne kicks off.
**You get to know before you must decide.**

- Etienne **OUT** -> start **Odunze** in FLEX.
- Etienne **active** -> leave it. `Q` players who dress usually play a normal workload.

**Kill condition:** Etienne under 7.0 AND opportunity under 12 — the same bar Week 2 set,
unchanged so the two weeks are comparable. Leaving an inactive Etienne in the lineup is
**not** a kill condition, it is an unforced error; the retro should record it separately.

### D4. RB — Henry + J. Williams, unchanged

Deadline **Sun 13:00** (Marks plays then). Proj 16.99 and 13.32 vs Marks 7.16,
Gainwell 6.74. Gap is ~6 points; nothing to discuss.

**Henry is the best-positioned player on the roster.** BAL favored by 3.5 -> peak RB
bucket (1.078x), AND the game total is **52.5, highest on the slate**, where RBs run
1.061x. Two independent tailwinds.

Williams and Ferguson are on the **underdog** side of that same game (RB dog 3-7 =
0.945x, TE = 0.953x). Mild drag, accepted — they are the only options at those slots.

**Kill condition:** Marks or Gainwell outscores Henry. Would mean the projection gap is
not real and RB2 deserves a weekly look rather than an assumption.

### D5. Raymond — trigger did NOT fire, stays benched

Pre-committed in Week 2: **6+ targets -> starts Week 3.** He got **5**. Missing by one
is missing. His 2021-25 record stands: 8+ target games in 2 of 78 career (2.6%).
Week 3 proj **4.94**, lowest on the roster. Chicago are 4.5-point home dogs vs PHI.

**Call:** bench. No new argument was offered, and the old trigger did not fire.
**Kill condition:** Raymond outscores both starting WRs. Beating one is variance.
**Trigger, re-committed unchanged:** 6+ targets in Week 3 -> starts Week 4.

### D6. Streaming — Chiefs DEF and Butker in. BOTH EXECUTED.

**The reasoning is positional, not player-specific.** K and DST are the only slots where
a weekly matchup swap is nearly free: one roster spot each, no opportunity cost, and
both were the worst-positioned starters on the roster.

**Chiefs DEF over Patriots DEF.** Yahoo DST scoring is dominated by points allowed
(`config/scoring.json`: 0 pts allowed = 10, 1-6 = 7, 7-13 = 4, **14-20 = 1**,
**21-27 = 0**).

| | opponent implied | tier | proj |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patriots (NE @ JAX, +3 dog) | **24.2** | 0 pts | 5.55 |
| **Chiefs** (KC @ MIA, -11.5) | **17.5** | 1 pt, near the 4-pt tier | **7.77** |

Corroborated independently by injury data, not just the line: MIA is without **Tyreek
Hill (knee, ACL)** with three more WRs `Q`, and **KC's defense has nobody on the week 3
report** (checked via `nflreadr::load_injuries()` — the Yahoo injuries export is
skill-positions-only and cannot answer this).

**Butker over McLaughlin.** KC implied **29.0** vs TB **20.5**; proj 9.06 vs 7.70.
Lower conviction, recorded as such: McLaughlin scored **16.00** in Week 2 and kicker
scoring is noisy. Taken because it is the same game environment as the DEF move and
costs nothing but a roster slot.

**Kill condition, both:** Patriots outscore Chiefs, or McLaughlin outscores Butker, **by
more than 3**. Under 3 is noise on positions this volatile. If BOTH dropped players win
by >3, streaming on implied totals is not working and the method needs review, not the
players.

### D7. No lineup swaps. Tested exhaustively.

All 16 legal bench-for-starter swaps were evaluated. **Every one loses projected points**;
the least-bad is Odunze for Sutton at **-1.13**. The lineup is projection-optimal.

Recorded because "we checked and there was nothing" is a result, and without it the
retro cannot tell a considered hold from an unconsidered one.

## 3. What to learn this week

Ranked. **n=3. Fit nothing.** These are questions to answer, not models to build.

1. **Does streaming K/DST on implied totals work?** D6 is the first deliberate test. Two
   swaps, both justified the same way, both with a >3 point kill bar. A clean answer here
   is worth more than any lineup decision, because it repeats every week for 13 weeks and
   the slots are otherwise dead weight. **This is the week's real experiment.**
2. **Does the game-script effect hold out of sample?** The 2024-25 measurement said RB
   favored 3-7 = 1.078x, WR flat, QB favored 10+ = 1.120x. Week 3 supplies three live
   tests: Henry (fav 3.5, high total), Mahomes (fav 11.5), Sutton (dog, WR -> should not
   matter). Record actual-vs-own-average for each, do not just record points.
3. **Does single-game concentration hurt?** Three starters in KC @ MIA, unplanned.
   Kill condition in §1. If it fires, correlation needs a penalty and not just a warning.
4. **Is the `Q` -> inactive contingency executed correctly?** Process, not outcome.
   Did we check at ~14:55 and act? Week 2's lesson was that lineup deadlines are set by
   replacements; this is the first week that knowledge is load-bearing in real time.
5. **Was Odunze right to stay benched twice?** D2 fired against us in Week 2 and we
   benched him again. If it fires again, the reasoning is wrong twice and Sutton's roster
   spot is the question, not the lineup slot.

Explicitly NOT being learned this week: anything about Raymond (trigger did not fire,
nothing changed), and anything requiring a model fit.

1. **Etienne `Q`.** Only live decision. Check ~Sun 14:55. See D3.
2. **DST is still unscored in R.** `score_player_week()` is per-player by design, so the
   Chiefs' actual points must be read off Yahoo for the retro. Week 2's DEF was worth
   **21.00, 14% of the winning total** — this gap now sits on a slot we actively manage.
3. **`proj` is frozen at 2026-09-23 values.** Yahoo revises on inactive news within the
   day (Adams moved 9.82 -> 12.32 in Week 2 once Nacua was ruled out); we have no such
   mechanism. Record the freeze-time value, which is what the decisions were made on.
4. **Do not trust `yahoo_week3_rosterchanges_injured_reserve.csv`.** 15% of its Sep 23
   rows list the same player as both "On" and "Off" IR — including Mahomes, Adams, Olave
   and Kamara, all demonstrably healthy. Use `yahoo_week3_injuries.csv` and
   `yahoo_week3_gamedaycalls.csv`, which agree with each other and with nflreadr.
